### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s).

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2ea604223a4136eb50af81b7b70669f09fb89f93`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **13** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2ea604223a4136eb50af81b7b70669f09fb89f93` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3fe28222a1e1655f7f1591be07e1563da30917a4` — the merge of head `483976d87fcab886af74a7c8d7d5966ead76d63f` into base `2ea604223a4136eb50af81b7b70669f09fb89f93`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3fe28222a1e1655f7f1591be07e1563da30917a4 && git checkout 3fe28222a1e1655f7f1591be07e1563da30917a4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2ea604223a4136eb50af81b7b70669f09fb89f93 483976d87fcab886af74a7c8d7d5966ead76d63f && git checkout -B drift-repro 2ea604223a4136eb50af81b7b70669f09fb89f93 && git merge --no-ff 483976d87fcab886af74a7c8d7d5966ead76d63f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2ea604223a4136eb50af81b7b70669f09fb89f93
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2ea604223a4136eb50af81b7b70669f09fb89f93` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `483976d87fcab886af74a7c8d7d5966ead76d63f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/business-unit-hierarchy-complete.integration.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/business-unit-graph.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/business-unit-hierarchy-reads-complete.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/team-graph.ts (`readMembershipToCompletion`, `holderReadRefusal`), packages/types/src/keyset-walk.ts (`keysetWalk`, `withCursor`), packages/types/src/object-absence.ts (`isObjectAbsentError`), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts (`expandRecipient`, `revokeRuleGrantsForRetiredRecipients`, `evaluateAllForRecord`, `evaluateAllRulesForObject`, `ruleReachesUser`), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/bu-tree-recompute.ts (`onGraphWrite`, `queueRegrant`), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/recipient-membership-recompute.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/ownership-queue-service.ts (`expandSpec`), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/business-unit-graph.test.ts (the hand-rolled engine the unit reads now walk through), the serial predecessor PR #29647 at `e0187d0f` (same two source files, its changeset), and the `.changeset/29655-business-unit-hierarchy-reads-refuse.md` declaration lines read under ②.

Face: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset; `--template --face narrowing`. Reviewed read-only from the diff against `main` at `2ea60422`, the card (body plus comments 6592460295, 6592611581, 6593642509), the head's check-runs, and the cited files at the head (`git show 483976d8:PATH`, REST `contents?ref=`). Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Check-runs on the head at review time (three polls, 02:15Z to 02:22Z):** 49 runs at the last poll, 32 `success`, 12 `skipped`, 5 `in_progress` (Test Core shards 2, 3, 4, 6, 8), 0 failures. Green: Lint · ESLint, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · workspace, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Check PR Size, Spec property liveness, Flag docs affected by code changes, Dogfood Regression Gate, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Build Core, Build Docs, Test Core shards 1, 5 and 7. The Test Core shards had not concluded, so the test-file pins below are judged from the code and the rig, not from a gate. The seat should read them green before landing.

**Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:**

1. **Sharing `BusinessUnitGraphService.seedIsUsable`: a failed `sys_business_unit` read throws instead of answering `false`.** Right. The read now goes through `readMembershipToCompletion` (team-graph.ts:183), whose catch returns `null` only for `isObjectAbsentError(err, 'sys_business_unit')` and otherwise throws `holderReadRefusal` (`[sharing] business unit 'ID' could not be read: REASON. A shortened or empty holder set would withhold or revoke …`). `seedRows?.[0]` on `null` is `undefined`, so absence still answers `false`. Both callers (`descendants`:98, `expandUnitMembers`:198) `await` it before their `cache.set`, so a thrown read sets nothing. The one-row-by-`id` lookup through a 10,000-row keyset page is correct: `withCursor` is never reached (the first page has no cursor), one row is shorter than `want`, the walk returns after one `find`.
2. **Sharing `descendants`: child units are read through the new private `readChildUnits` in pages of 1,000 (`CHILD_UNIT_PAGE_ROWS`) to completion; a failed read throws before `cache.descendants.set`.** Right. `readMembershipToCompletion` with `fields: []` projects `['id']`; `keysetWalk` has no `max`, so a parent with more than 1,000 active children is read in further pages, each AND-ed with `{ id: { $gt: cursor } }` through `$and` (keyset-walk.ts `withCursor`), which composes with the caller's `parent_business_unit_id` / `active: { $ne: false }` / `organization_id` predicate rather than overwriting any of them. A non-advancing cursor sets `truncated` and `readMembershipToCompletion` throws `WALK_INCOMPLETE`, so the subtree never silently shortens. Absence returns `null` → `[]` for that parent. The loop is the same breadth-first `seen` / `queue`, so the descent's shape and dedupe are unchanged.
3. **Sharing: nothing is cached after a failed read.** Right, for all three maps touched by this diff: `descendants` sets only after the loop completes (:116) or after a non-failed unusable seed (:100); `expandUnitMembers` sets only after `seedIsUsable` returned and `readMembers` returned (:212); `expandUsers` sets only after `descendants` and `readMembers` returned (:236). The absent-or-inactive seed is still cached as `[]`, which is the card's own stipulation (absence is an answer, not a failure). The `cache.head` map (`headOf`) is untouched by the diff, see ③.
4. **Approvals `expandBusinessUnitUsers`: the seed catch-all becomes absence-only.** Right. `businessUnitIsLive` (:3293) is unchanged and already throws; the new catch returns `[]` on `isObjectAbsentError(err, 'sys_business_unit')` and otherwise throws `holderReadRefusal('business unit ID in organization ORG', err)`, the driver error on `cause`. An inactive or missing unit still answers `[]` (`if (!live) return []`).
5. **Approvals: the descent reads through the new private `readRowsToCompletion` in pages of 1,000.** Right. `readRowsToCompletion` is `readHoldersToCompletion`'s walk with the projection and page size lifted to parameters and the row collection returned instead of the `user_id` set; `readHoldersToCompletion` now calls it with `['user_id']` and `HOLDER_PAGE_ROWS` and maps `null` to `[]`, so the member read of #29647 answers exactly as before. The descent passes `fields: []` → `['id']`, `CHILD_UNIT_PAGE_ROWS`, and the existing `businessUnitOrgScope` predicate as the walk's `where`. `where` (not `filter`) is the key `businessUnitIsLive` and the #29647 member read already pass to the same `engine.find`, so the switch from the old `filter:` spelling is safe. `kids ?? []` keeps absence as "no children".
6. **One refusal sentence, `holderReadRefusal(scope, err)`.** Right: the string is the one `readHoldersToCompletion` carried since #29362, moved to a module function and reused by the seed catch and the walk; no wording changes, `cause` preserved.
7. **Public surface.** No export is added to or removed from any package index; `packages/spec` is untouched; `readChildUnits`, `readRowsToCompletion` and `holderReadRefusal` (approvals) are private / module-local; `CHILD_UNIT_PAGE_ROWS` is a module constant in each plugin. The only observable change of kind is on the failure arm: a failed `sys_business_unit` read, which answered `[]` / `false`, now rejects. That is a narrowing of an answer the spec never declared, not a declared capability removed at a consumer.

**The brief's four questions:** a failed unit-table read (seed check or child-unit descent) can no longer answer "nobody" at either site; nothing is cached after a failed read at either site; absence (`isObjectAbsentError` on `sys_business_unit`) still answers `[]` / `false` at both sites, both for an unregistered object and for a dropped table (the test rigs pin both forms); descents read to completion past 1,000 rows at both sites through the shared `keysetWalk` with no `max`, and the two test files count 2 driver reads for 1,001 children against 1 for 999.

**Tests, judged from the rig.** Both new files run a real `ObjectQL` + `SqlDriver` over in-memory SQLite with the shipped `SysBusinessUnit` / `SysBusinessUnitMember` and scramble unit ids against creation order, so the 1,001-child pin exercises the seek past the last `id` (`$gt` on the cursor), not insertion order. The fault is injected at the driver's `find` for `sys_business_unit` and keyed on whether the query carries `parent_business_unit_id`, so the seed and descent faults are distinct and the member reads run real. The sharing rig's `failUnitReads(which, times)` takes the driver's real `find` once at boot, so the not-cached pins (fail once, then read again on the same instance) wrap the real method rather than the previous spy. The read counter matches `select … from sys_business_unit … parent_business_unit_id` with `ROOT` among the bindings, so it counts only the descent's reads of ROOT's children. The approvals rig asserts the caller's view through `resolveApproverSpec` (the literal `department:bu_root` plus one `could not be expanded — a directory or read-filter lookup failed` warning whose `error` names `SQLITE_IOERR`), and that absence of the object leaves no failure warning. The four ablations in the PR body each put one catch back and turn exactly the two pins for that site red; the record does not re-run them.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/29655-business-unit-hierarchy-reads-refuse.md` declares `@objectstack/plugin-sharing: patch` and `@objectstack/plugin-approvals: patch`, carries `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, an `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker, and a `**BREAKING** only where a sys_business_unit read fails` paragraph under a `fix(plugins)!:` subject. The PR body carries the same two declaration lines. The diff publishes no new or removed export, no schema key, no metadata change; the only consumer-visible change is the failure arm's kind. `patch` with the `!` marker and the `(narrowing)` arm is exactly the level and the lines the serial predecessor #29647 (`e0187d0f`, `.changeset/29606-business-unit-member-reads-complete.md`) landed for the same two packages on the same shape, and `Check Changeset` is green on the head. The changeset's four claims about callers are each true in the cited code: sharing's rule pass fails and its grants stay (④, bullets 1 to 3); approvals' slot falls back to its literal with the failed-read warning (`resolveApproverSpec` catch at approval-service.ts:2631, `resolveExpressionApprovers` catch at :2898 via `warnExpansionFailed`); a queue BU spec contributes nobody and logs once (`OwnershipQueueService.expandSpec` `.catch` → `warnOnce` → `[]`, ownership-queue-service.ts:309); a missing object is still nobody. The semver level and the `Clause-②:` line match the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

From the os-dev-report (comment 6593642509), `open_questions: []`, `security_findings: none`, and two `out_of_scope_findings`:

1. **`BusinessUnitGraphService.headOf` still turns a failed `sys_business_unit` read into `null` and caches it in `cache.head` for the pass** (business-unit-graph.ts:264-282, untouched by the diff). Judged: a follow-up card, not this PR's scope, and not a FAIL. The card's "Wanted" names the seed check and the child-unit descent, the two reads that feed a recipient set; `headOf` names one `manager_user_id`. On this tree it has no production consumer: `grep -rn "\.headOf("` across `packages/` (test files excluded) finds only the `IBusinessUnitGraphService` contract in `packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts` and the dogfood authz matrix. No grant is computed or revoked from it. It is still the same family (a swallowed read cached as an answer for the pass), so it should be filed as its own p3 card against `business-unit-graph.ts` (`headOf` → refuse on failure, absence → `null`, nothing cached after a failed read), with `managerOf`'s standalone-fallback catch (:314, `sys_user` read → `null`) noted alongside since it sits in the same file. The seat files it; the dev's "noted, not filed" is answered here by escalation, not by leaving it in the PR body alone.
2. **Deviations:** `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` touched outside the claim's file surface (one sentence beside #29647's member-read sentence) — a prose face, the seat's; its content agrees with the approvals change under ① bullet 4 (a `department` entry keeps its literal and logs the failed-read line when the unit or child-unit read fails). Commit messages without a card trailer and WIP subjects squashed by the PR title — the PR body carries `Fixes #29655` and the seat line, so the merge commit will. No action.

No other flag. `ownership-queue-service.ts` is untouched as the claim required (#29604's). The check-runs still in progress at review time are named under ①; this record judges the code and leaves the seat to read the shards green before landing.

### ④ Design judgment

Each in-scope file against the code it cites and the scenario the card accepts it against (a `sys_business_unit` read fails during a business-unit graph write; 1,001 child units; absence), with the attempts to break it:

**`packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/business-unit-graph.ts`** — holds.
- *Callers that relied on the old swallow.* `SharingRuleService.expandRecipient` (sharing-rule-service.ts:2105) constructs a fresh `BusinessUnitGraphService` per call with no shared `cache`, awaits `expandUnitMembers` / `expandUsers`, then `warnOnEmptyUnitExpansion`. A throw now skips the "expands to NO recipients" warning, which is right: a failed read is not an empty expansion. Every reconciler that reaches it is per-rule best-effort: `evaluateAllForRecord` (:1416 try/catch per rule, warns `record reconcile failed for rule`), `evaluateAllRulesForObject` (:1458, warns `object reconcile failed for rule`), `ruleReachesUser` → `reconcileRuleForUser` under the recipient-membership recompute's per-rule catch (recipient-membership-recompute.ts:317). `evaluateRule` called directly from a rule write propagates, as it has since #29647 for the member read — the predecessor's accepted shape, not a new exposure.
- *The scenario itself.* `bu-tree-recompute.ts` `onGraphWrite` (:271) runs, per affected rule, `revokeRuleGrantsForRetiredRecipients` inside its own try/catch and then `queueRegrant`. In `revokeRuleGrantsForRetiredRecipients` (sharing-rule-service.ts:1599) `desired = new Set(await this.expandRecipient(rule))` is awaited before any `engine.delete`, so a thrown seed or descent read leaves every `sys_record_share` row of that rule in place and the hook warns `business-unit revocation failed — this rule may still grant access … until the next reconcile`. The queued re-grant (`evaluateRule` → `evaluateResolvedRule` → `desiredGrantsForRule` → `expandRecipient` at :2081) throws before `reconcile` is entered, so nothing is granted or revoked, and the queue's error handler warns `business-unit re-grant failed`. The outer catch keeps the operator's write from failing. This is exactly the posture the card wants: a refusal grants nothing and revokes nothing. Before this diff the same outage set `desired` to the empty set and deleted every grant.
- *Per-pass cache keying.* `DeptCache` is keyed by unit id with `organizationId` fixed per instance; no caller on this tree passes a shared `cache` across instances or organizations (`sharing-rule-service.ts`, `ownership-queue-service.ts` construct without one). The three maps touched set only on a completed answer (① bullet 3). The absent-seed `[]` is still cached, by design.
- *The one keyset walk.* No new walk spelling: both unit reads call `readMembershipToCompletion`, the shared `keysetWalk` of #29362 / #29503 / #29647. The hand-rolled engine in `business-unit-graph.test.ts`, whose `sys_business_unit` side ignores `orderBy` and `limit` but whose `matches` models `$and` / `$gt` generically, still satisfies the walk (a page shorter than `want` ends it), so the 25 existing pins are not broken by routing the unit side through it.
- *Nits, no action owed:* `seedIsUsable` now issues an `orderBy id` and a 10,000-row page for a one-row-by-`id` lookup where `limit: 1` sufficed; correct, marginally heavier, and it keeps the refusal and absence posture in one helper. The sharing subject omits the organization that the approvals subject carries (`in organization 'ORG'`); cosmetic.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts`** — holds.
- *Callers that relied on the old swallow.* `resolveApproverSpec` (:2613) and `resolveExpressionApprovers` (:2884) both wrap the expansion in the directory catch (:2631 → `directoryFailure`, :2898 → `warnExpansionFailed`), so an approval step degrades to the literal slot plus the warning, never to a crash and never to a shrunk slate. `decisionOutputValueRefusal` (:4751) calls `businessUnitIsLive` directly under its own catch → `undefined`, unchanged. No other caller of `expandBusinessUnitUsers` exists.
- *Error propagation.* The seed refusal wraps the driver error with `cause`; the descent refusal comes from `readRowsToCompletion`'s catch with the walk's scope sentence (`the child units of business unit 'P' in organization 'O'`), so the warning names which unit's read failed. A mid-walk failure on a second page throws with nothing returned (the `rows` array is local). `walk.truncated` throws the existing incomplete-walk sentence.
- *Factoring.* `readHoldersToCompletion` is now a thin projection over `readRowsToCompletion`; `null` → `[]` keeps the #29647 absence answer for every holder read (`sys_team_member`, `sys_user_position`, `sys_member`, `sys_business_unit_member`), and the `user_id` dedupe is unchanged. `holderReadRefusal` moves the sentence to one place without changing it.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/business-unit-hierarchy-reads-complete.test.ts`** — holds against the card's four pins per site: failed seed read refuses on all three entry points and is not cached (fail once, next call answers the real set, for both widths); failed descent read refuses on `descendants` and `expandUsers`, is not cached, and leaves `expandUnitMembers` untouched (a control that proves the fault is keyed to the descent); 1,001 children → every unit and every member, 2 reads, against 999 → 1 read; absence by unregistered object and by dropped table answers `[]` on all three. Real engine, real seek.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/business-unit-hierarchy-complete.integration.test.ts`** — holds against the same four pins plus the caller's view: refusal text per site, literal slot plus one `department` failure warning carrying `SQLITE_IOERR`, 1,001 children → every member on the slate with 2 reads (control 1), absence → `[]` and the literal with no failure warning.

**Must-fix:** none.
**Should-fix:** none in this tree. The `headOf` / `managerOf` swallow is escalated under ③ as a follow-up card, not a change to this PR.
